text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is common in senior banking risk roles and is, by itself, weak evidence. Raising it as your headline point is easy to dismiss and makes you look like you're inferring bias from demographics rather than facts.

The stronger material is elsewhere. "Broad experience of regulatory affairs" is a genuine requirement for this role — model approval, supervisory engagement — so the panel may honestly have valued it over technical depth. But the vagueness of that phrase, against your PhD and nine years, is worth probing. And the unanswered request for written reasons is the real problem: chase it in writing, cite any applicable right to reasons, set a deadline.

Panel composition becomes relevant context later, if the reasons don't hold up.
